requirement: REQ-001, REQ-011 (also REQ-006/REQ-013 cycle-exact frame timing)
root_cause: uart_tx accepts a byte in IDLE but keeps tx high in ST_START until the next free-running tick16, so the start bit begins up to baud_div cycles late and tx_ready stays low longer than one frame time.
evidence: All TX tests fail on the first cycle after accept: 'tx mismatch: expected 0 actual 1' (e.g. cycle 5/6/11 at baud_div=1,27,3,0,4; expected all tx=0 tx_ready=0, actual tx=1 tx_ready=0). In rtl/uart_tx.v ST_IDLE sets state_q<=ST_START without setting tx_q<=0; ST_START only sets tx_q<=0 when tick16 && tx_q (the 'aligned start' branch), and then counts a further 16 ticks. ref_model.py sets tx=bits[0]=0 on the accept edge and ends the frame exactly 16*div*nbits cycles after accept. Even at div=1 tx falls two edges after accept instead of one.
expected: The cycle after the accepted tx_valid&tx_ready edge shows tx=0 with tx_ready=0, each bit lasts exactly 16*baud_div clk, and tx_ready returns to 1 exactly 10 or 11 bit periods after accept.
actual: tx remains 1 until the next tick16 (0..baud_div cycles later, at div=1 one cycle later), so the start bit is delayed and the whole frame plus tx_ready low window are longer than 10/11 bit periods by that delay.
suggested_fix: In ST_IDLE on accept drive tx_q<=0 immediately (start bit begins the cycle after accept) and time the start bit as exactly 16*max(baud_div,1) clk from accept, e.g. with a TX-local phase alignment or a divider that restarts on accept, rather than waiting for the free-running shared tick16. Do not restart the shared baud_gen counter, since uart_rx uses it. Keep stop bit exactly 16 ticks for REQ-013 and tx_ready low until stop completes.
